newsitem.title: UK: Europe life, pension sales to hit $500 bln - report.
newsitem.headline: Europe life, pension sales to hit $500 bln - report.

text.p: Sales of life insurance and pensions in Europe are set to top $500 billion by the end of the century, management consultant Datamonitor said in a report on Tuesday.

"The European life insurance and pensions market is forecast to continue to grow rapidly over the next four years. Datamonitor predicts that it will be worth $502.9 billion in the year 2000, which represents average growth of 12.2 percent each year."
Life and pensions sales amounted to $317.3 billion in Europe in 1995, Datamonitor said in its report "European Life Insurance and Pensions".
Only eight companies have a market share of more than two percent of total European business and foreign companies have made little impact in the most attractive European markets, the report added.
Growth will be driven by government action to encourage private savings, greater awareness among consumers and the increased marketing ability of financial institutions.
France, Germany and the UK will account for over half the European life and pensions market by 2000, but countries in southern Europe will show the strongest growth, Datamonitor said.
The biggest market players are Axa/UAP with 5.9 percent, CNP with 4.7 percent, Allianz with 3.7 percent, Generali with 3.0 percent and Swiss Life with 2.5 percent.

"Almost all insurance groups in Europe, and some from the U.S., are looking at increasing their share of the European life and pensions market," Alan Leach, manager of Datamonitor's financial services practices area said.

"However, the number of aspiring entrants exceeds the opportunities available and some competitors may be left on the sidelines...There are rich pickings to be had, but only the fortunate few will profit," he added.
